notes: X / Twitter web UI. The user is logged in; tools act as them. Read tools (/x_me, /x_timeline, /x_get_tweet) are safe; /x_compose_draft and /x_like_tweet have side effects but are reversible; /x_post_now is irreversible — it publishes a tweet. Many pages share selectors; if a tool returns count: 0, you're probably on the wrong route — navigate first with /x_open_home, /x_open_profile, or /x_open_tweet.

tools.description: Return info about the logged-in user: handle, display name, profile URL. Works on any X page.

Read visible tweets from the current page (home feed, profile, search results, etc). Returns text, author handle, timestamp, permalink, and reply/retweet/like counts. Set limit to cap the number returned (default 10).
On a /[handle]/status/[id] page, return the focal tweet + its visible replies. Navigate to the tweet first if needed (e.g. via /x_open_tweet).
Navigate to the home timeline (/home). The handler does not wait for full load — pair with /wait_for if you need to be sure.
Navigate to a user's profile page by handle (without leading @).
Navigate to a specific tweet. Provide either { handle, id } or { url }.
Run a search query on x.com. Navigates to /search?q=...&src=typed_query.

Open the compose dialog (if not already open) and fill the tweet textarea WITHOUT posting. Returns once the text is in the box. Call /x_post_now afterwards to publish. The compose modal uses DraftJS so this tool uses execCommand('insertText') — more reliable than direct value assignment.

text.description: Tweet body. Max ~280 chars for non-premium accounts.

tools.description: Publish the currently-drafted tweet by clicking the active Post button. Irreversible. Call /x_compose_draft first to fill the textarea. Returns immediately after clicking — pair with a short /wait_for if you need to confirm submission.
Like (or unlike) a visible tweet by its index on the current page. Use /x_timeline to enumerate first and pick the index. Default action 'toggle' — like if not liked, unlike if already liked.
Navigate to /notifications. Pair with /x_timeline to read the notifications list as 'tweets' (they share article markup for mentions/replies).
Navigate to /i/bookmarks. Use /x_timeline afterwards to read the bookmarked tweets.
